newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Strong debt market sends NZ shares to firmer close.
newsitem.headline: Strong debt market sends NZ shares to firmer close.

text.p: * Rally in debt market encourages equities buyers
* Uncertain political situation not worrying share market
The New Zealand share market, encouraged by a strong debt market, staged a surprisingly strong performance on Monday, brokers said.

The top 40 index ended 19.47 up at 2,367.89 as indicator 90-day bank bills rallied 17 basis points. Volume was also a healthy $80 million, boosted by a big line in Telecom -- 3.8 million shares traded at $7.45.
Telecom ended four cents up at that price.
Other leaders were also stronger apart from Lion Nathan which was down two at $3.59.
Brierley Investments was up three cents to $1.29, while Carter Holt Harvey rose four to $3.28, and Fletcher Paper rose three to $2.55.
Doyle Paterson Brown broker Philip Solarz said the uncertain political situation, with no government formed since the October 12 election, did not appear to be deterring investors.
Apart from the turnover in Telecom, he said there were few highlights. -- Simon Louisson 64 4 4714 276
